verses.text: In the twelfth year of King Ahaz's reign over Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for nine years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, though he didn't go as far as the kings of Israel before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him. Hoshea became his subject and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea was plotting against him. Hoshea had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped paying the tribute he'd paid every year. So the king of Assyria arrested him and locked him up in prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land and laid siege to Samaria for three years.
In Hoshea's ninth year, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and took the Israelites away to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, along the Habor River in Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes.
This happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them out of Egypt and rescued them from Pharaoh king of Egypt. They began to worship other gods.
They adopted the customs of the nations the LORD had driven out before them and the practices the kings of Israel had introduced.
In secret the Israelites did things that were wrong against the LORD their God. They built high places in every town, from lonely watchtowers to fortified cities.
They set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
They burned incense at all those high places, just like the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of them. Their wicked actions provoked the LORD to anger.
They served idols even though the LORD had told them, “You must not do this.”

Through every prophet and seer the LORD warned Israel and Judah: “Turn back from your evil ways. Keep my commands and statutes in keeping with the law I gave your ancestors and sent to you through my servants the prophets.”
But they refused to listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who didn't trust the LORD their God.

They rejected his statutes, the covenant he'd made with their ancestors, and his warnings to them. They chased worthless things and became worthless themselves. They imitated the nations around them, though the LORD had told them not to.
They abandoned all the commands of the LORD their God. They cast two calf idols, made an Asherah pole, bowed down to the whole host of heaven, and served Baal.
They made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and spells, and sold themselves to do evil in the LORD's sight, provoking him to anger.
The LORD was so angry with Israel that he removed them from his sight. Only the tribe of Judah remained.
Even Judah didn't keep the commands of the LORD their God. They followed the practices Israel had introduced.
The LORD rejected all Israel's descendants. He afflicted them and handed them over to raiders until he'd thrown them out of his sight.
When he tore Israel away from David's house, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. Jeroboam pulled Israel away from following the LORD and led them into grave sin.
The Israelites kept committing all the sins Jeroboam had committed. They didn't turn from them
until the LORD removed Israel from his sight, just as he'd warned through all his servants the prophets. Israel was taken from its own land into Assyria, where the people remain to this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took over Samaria and lived in its towns.
When they first settled there, they didn't honor the LORD. So the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

The king of Assyria was told, “The people you moved into the towns of Samaria don't know the law of the god of that land. He's sent lions among them, and the lions are killing them because they don't know his law.”
The king of Assyria ordered, “Send back one of the priests you took from there. Let him live there and teach the people the law of the god of the land.”
So one of the priests who had been taken from Samaria came back and lived in Bethel. He taught them how to honor the LORD.
Still, each nation made its own gods and set them in the shrines the Samaritans had built at the high places in the towns where they now lived.
The people from Babylon made Succoth Benoth, those from Cuth made Nergal, and those from Hamath made Ashima.
The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the people from Sepharvaim burned their children in the fire for their gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
They honored the LORD too and appointed people from among themselves to serve as priests who sacrificed for them at the shrines on the high places.
They honored the LORD while serving their own gods, following the customs of the nations from which they'd been taken.
To this day they still follow their old customs. They don't truly honor the LORD or obey the statutes, rulings, law, and commands the LORD gave the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
The LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them, “Don't fear other gods or bow down to them, serve them, or offer sacrifices to them.
Honor the LORD, who brought you out of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm. Bow down to him and offer your sacrifices to him.
Always be careful to follow the statutes, rulings, law, and commands he wrote for you. Don't fear other gods.
Don't forget the covenant I made with you, and don't fear other gods.
Honor the LORD your God, and he'll rescue you from all your enemies.”
They refused to listen and kept following their old customs.
These nations honored the LORD while serving their carved images. Their children and grandchildren did the same. To this day they do what their ancestors did.
